issues.current: 'Annual; licenses expire at the end of the calendar year (Dec 31)'. The renewal fee is assumed equal to the $350 initial fee.
issues.correct: G.S. 122C-23(e) says initial licenses are valid for up to 15 months, then renewed annually and expiring at the end of the calendar year. The renewal fee amount is still unverified.

issues.current: '10A NCAC 27G .5600 (staffing rule text not retrieved)'. The model relies on a 2018 DHHS report for '1 staff per 6 individuals'.
issues.correct: The staffing rule is 10A NCAC 27G .5602 (Staff). Its paragraph (b) requires at least one staff member present at all times when any adult client is on the premises, unless the client's plan documents otherwise. The modeled coverage (at least one awake staff 24/7, up to two) meets that floor. The ratio and overnight paragraphs (c)/(d) were not retrievable, so the '1:6' claim is unverified.
issues.evidence: A DHSR statement of deficiencies quotes .5602(b): 'A minimum of one staff member shall be present at all times when any adult client is on the premises, except when the client's treatment or habilitation plan documents…'. The same rule is titled '.5602 Supervised Living – Staff'.
issues.fix: Change the cite to '10A NCAC 27G .5602' and add the 'one staff present at all times' minimum. Read paragraphs (c)/(d) before finalizing schedules. No staffing violation was found in the modeled hours: 973 / 1,217 / 1,460 hours per home per month all exceed 730 hours of one-staff 24/7 coverage.

issues.json_path: staffing.* (direct support wage_hourly 17.0 × coverage hours) and payroll_burden
issues.current: A flat $17.00/hr × coverage hours, with a 17.8% burden. There is no overtime or relief-coverage premium.
issues.correct: BLS-sourced wages are higher. The NC CNA median is $18.49/hr, which is confirmed, and the NC RN median is $84,350/yr ($40.56/hr), also confirmed. $17.00 is above the $7.25 NC minimum wage, so there is no wage-floor violation. 24/7 coverage across part-time and full-time DSPs usually creates FLSA overtime (1.5× over 40 hrs/week) or sick/vacation relief hours that are not costed.
issues.evidence: CaresLink (May 2025 BLS data): NC nursing assistant median $38,460 / $18.49 per hour. NC registered nurse median $84,350 / $40.56 per hour.
issues.fix: Keep $17.00 only as a low case. Use $18.49 as the base wage, since the model's own loss figures at $18.49 show thin or negative margins. Add an overtime/relief factor (for example 5–10% of DSP hours at 1.5×) as a mandatory cost. Raleigh-Cary $19.29 and NC all-occupation $47,970 were not independently verified (unverifiable).

Federal fee 'when applicable'. The NC Medicaid enrollment page confirms '$100 NC application fee during enrollment and re-verification' and re-verification every five years.
issues.fix: For the 2- and 3-home configurations, confirm with NCTracks whether the $100 is charged per site or per tax ID. If per site, raise the high case to $100 × the number of homes. The federal fee remains 'confirm at enrollment' (unverifiable here).
